title: Residual-aware layer scale harmonization and calibration sweep for FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When generating FP8/INT8 quantization profiles for a set of open models (Llama 2 variants, Mistral-7B, Qwen-7B), we observe model-specific accuracy regressions caused by a) residual-branch scale divergence and b) isolated activation outliers in attention projection and feedforward layers. Current per-layer max-clipping followed by a single global rescale produces brittle profiles that either under-quantize (high latency/cost) or underflow important tails (quality regressions).

Goal: Implement a residual-aware harmonization step in the calibration workflow that adjusts per-layer scale factors considering residual accumulation paths and headwise activation distributions. Combine this with an automated calibration sweep that produces candidate FP8 and INT8 profiles, ranks them by accuracy-cost tradeoff across representative prompt sets, and promotes the safe default profiles to our model catalog.

This ticket covers design, implementation, benchmarks, and rollout gating for the harmonization algorithm and calibration sweep tooling for the three target model families.
acceptance_criteria: New calibration pipeline produces FP8/INT8 profiles for Llama/Mistral/Qwen families with no >1.5% loss in core LM perplexity on validation prompts vs FP16 baseline
Profiles demonstrate stable per-token logprob distributions (KS distance < 0.03) and no more than 5% increase in downstream instruction-following task failure rate compared to baseline
CI includes a regression test that runs a small representative sweep and fails if any candidate profile introduces high-severity hallucination regressions on the prompt corpus
Profiles uploaded to model catalog with metadata (algorithm version, calibration seeds, hardware fingerprint) and rollout gating enabled in console
Documentation and a short how-to for customers describing when to select FP8 vs INT8 profile and expected tradeoffs
implementation_steps: Design harmonization algorithm: compute per-layer effective scale by combining activation percentile (e.g., 99.9th), residual path amplification factor, and headwise variance multiplier
Extend existing calib-harness to collect residual path traces and headwise activation histograms during calibration runs on representative dataset
Implement per-layer residual-aware rescale operator that can be toggled for FP8/INT8 pipeline (runtime-agnostic output: JSON quant profile)
Integrate hybrid clipping: headwise soft-clipping for attention projections + layerwise hard-rescale for FFN and residual addends
Add a multi-dimensional sweep runner that explores clipping percentiles, headwise attenuation, and global rescale annealing; export candidate profiles with metadata and cost estimates
Run sweeps on dedicated infra (small GPU cluster), collect accuracy/cost metrics, and produce ranked candidates
Add automated validation: synthetic stress tests (long-form generation + adversarial prompts) and downstream evals (RAG QA and instruction following), integrate into CI gating
Promote best candidates into model catalog and add rollback policy in console for any customer-visible regression
implementation_notes: Prior experiments show attention-projection heads often contain narrow extreme outliers that dominate naive per-layer max; addressing headwise tails reduces overall clamp aggressiveness

Residual accumulation: multiple small rescale errors compound across layers when residual branches are large; algorithm should estimate amplification by tracing a small set of tokens through residual summations
Prefer percentile-based statistics (99.9/99.99) over absolute max to avoid single-sample spikes; use running medians across seeds to improve robustness
FP8 behavior constraint: exponent/overflow boundaries require conservative headwise attenuation for attention projections on Qwen models observed during earlier runs
Keep generated profiles hardware-fingerprintable (CUDA version, kernel selection tag) so we can differentiate calibration artifacts tied to kernel numerics
Avoid large runtime changes; output is a JSON quant profile that the inference runtime consumes unchanged — runtime fallback logic will choose a compatible numeric path if kernel support missing
test_plan: Unit tests for harmonization math (edge cases: zero-residual, extremely skewed heads)
Integration test: full calibration sweep on a downsampled Llama-2-7B weight snapshot with fixed random seeds
Accuracy validation: run downstream evals (SQuAD-style QA, summarization ROUGE, instruction-following pass/fail) comparing FP16, FP8-profile-A, INT8-profile-B
Performance check: measure per-token latency and memory consumption on dedicated GPU instance and ensure no >15% latency regression vs existing profiles
CI gating: daily smoke sweep that verifies no new promoted profile regresses on the core prompt corpus
Manual review: schedule a cross-team calibration review with Applied ML and Runtime teams to inspect candidate failures and decide rollout
dependencies: runtime-1.19 - runtime must accept new profile fields (residual_scale_hint, headwise_attenuation)
